clue.text: Pressed about part of UK being penalised

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: pressed on something is pushed it
NI is Northern Ireland, a constituent part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure about a region of Britain finds they are being punished.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is the part of the UK abbreviated in crosswords; it sits inside the word for pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be punished is to have a penalty imposed, a direct synonym of penalised.

clue.text: Place for studying part of Bible? Everything, really

blocks.note: UNI is short for university
the Bible is divided into chapters and verses

explanation.surface: A seminary where you study scripture is, it seems, the whole world to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: UNI + VERSE gives UNIVERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is the totality of all existing matter and space, literally everything there is.

clue.text: Plea for another is not sincere, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements the letters could take

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cynic's remark that pleading on someone else's behalf is a hollow gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercession is the act of intervening or praying on behalf of someone else, a plea made for another.

clue.text: Wants one footballer for team in hurry

blocks.note: a side lacking one player out of eleven has only ten men
a football team is eleven, so one short leaves ten

explanation.surface: A manager desperately needs one more player to complete the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Needing one footballer to make up a team of eleven means one HAS TEN; together HASTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to move quickly or make haste, so it serves as the verb hurry.

clue.text: Statistical information at short notice turned over

indicators.note: short says the word for notice is cut down to an abbreviated form
something turned over is upended, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
an advertisement is a notice, and AD is its short form

explanation.surface: Figures handed over at the last minute get flipped around.
explanation.walkthrough: AT + AD reads backwards as DATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for analysis, the stuff of statistics.

clue.text: Followed heartless lady with determination

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is cut away, leaving only the outside of the word

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
the first and last letters of lady

explanation.surface: Someone tailed a callous woman relentlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: DOGGED + LY gives DOGGEDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggedly means persistently and tenaciously, acting with grim determination.

clue.text: Old Bank of England, initially, as producer of notes

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in turn

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: The old Bank of England as a printer of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes look like banknotes from the Bank; they are musical notes from a woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, so it produces musical notes.

clue.text: Pressure on hot line in airport

blocks.note: putting the heat on someone is applying pressure
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: Stressful heat on a queue at a busy terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAT + H + ROW gives HEATHROW, London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is the largest airport serving London.

clue.text: King entering a social event, accomplished and charming

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the royal letter goes into the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
R for Rex, Latin for king
accomplished means capable

explanation.surface: A monarch arriving at a party proves skilled and delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: R enters A DO ABLE to give ADORABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and lovable, a close synonym of charming.

clue.text: Meat provided by Americans serving tea, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by their sound when spoken

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers; the phrase with tea is spoken as one word

explanation.surface: US soldiers bring a hot drink along with a meal of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat here is the core of an argument, as in 'the meat of the matter', not food.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist is the essential substance of something, its meat in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Result of splitting up in toughest range men tackled

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found running across the end of toughest, all of range and men, and the first letter of tackled

explanation.surface: A rugged team brought down on the hardest terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the state of being alienated, the outcome when a couple or family separates.

clue.text: Like John, Paul, or George, but not Ringo, speaking briefly?

definitions.text: Like John, Paul, or George, but not Ringo

blocks.clueFragment: Like John, Paul, or George, but not Ringo
blocks.note: first meaning: having one syllable, as those three Beatles' names do, unlike two-syllable Ringo
second meaning: curt, using few words

explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles look like the point, but the clue counts syllables in their first names.
explanation.definitionFit: A monosyllabic word has one syllable, and a monosyllabic speaker answers tersely in short words.

clue.text: District in which prince relocated court

indicators.note: relocated means moved to a new position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A royal moves his court to a new part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is a defined area or district, as in a shopping or police precinct.

clue.text: Two portions of pasta exchanged for Spanish food

indicators.note: exchanged means the two sections swap places with each other

blocks.note: the word split into two sections, PAS and TA

explanation.surface: Two helpings of Italian pasta are traded for a Spanish meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the halves of PAS-TA to get TA-PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury dishes served in Spain, typically with drinks.

clue.text: One who doesn't believe measure of yarn's quality

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who denies, pronounced deny-er
second meaning: the unit of fineness of silk or nylon thread, as on stockings

explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling covers two words: one who denies, and the hosiery unit pronounced den-ee-ay.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier rejects a claim, while the denier is the unit grading fibre weight in stockings and tights.

clue.text: Sides of Trent or other English river

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Trent are both T

explanation.surface: The banks of the Trent, or of some other river in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The two outer letters of Trent are a pair of Ts, spelt out as TEES. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is an English river other than the Trent, flowing to the North Sea at Middlesbrough.

clue.text: Member silenced following point of order?

definitions.text: Member silenced following point of order?

blocks.clueFragment: Member silenced following point of order?
blocks.note: surface reading: an MP ruled out of order and told to be quiet in Parliament
setter's reading: a monk keeping a rule of his religious order, which requires near-total silence

explanation.walkthrough: Point of order sounds like parliamentary procedure, but the order is a monastic one whose members keep silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a Cistercian monk of an order famous for its vow of silence.

clue.text: Fully successful candidate left within a year

indicators.note: within says these letters go inside the abbreviated year

blocks.note: taken as written
a candidate who wins an election becomes a Member of Parliament
L is the abbreviation for left
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A winning election candidate quit within twelve months, satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: MP + L goes within A Y to give AMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Amply means in abundant measure, so fully or more than sufficiently.

clue.text: Writhing in agony, holding front of nose, becoming tiresome

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters contort into a new order
front of means only the leading letter of the following word is taken
holding means gripping something inside, so one letter is placed within

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange
first letter of nose

explanation.surface: Someone clutching their nose in pain is getting on everyone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoying means irritating, and something tiresome wears out one's patience.

clue.text: Screen broadcast extending over hour

indicators.note: extending over means stretching around, so the outer word covers the letter

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, to sow
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A TV programme that overruns by an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast looks like television, but here it is the farming sense of scattering seed. SOW goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to show it, as a cinema or channel does with a film.

clue.text: No longer acting, having left old coach

blocks.note: someone who has gone off has left
a stagecoach, shortened to stage, was a horse-drawn coach of old

explanation.surface: An actor retires after leaving an old trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach is the vehicle, not a trainer. OFF + STAGE gives OFFSTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor offstage is out of view of the audience and so not performing at that moment.

clue.text: Case I deposited in part of London

indicators.note: deposited in means placed inside, so the single letter is put within the place name

blocks.note: Acton is a district of west London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A briefcase I left somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Case is a legal case, not luggage. I goes into ACTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit, which is also called a case in court.

clue.text: Make easier, having second hint provided inside

indicators.note: inside says these letters are placed within the word for hint

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to imply is to hint
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Getting a second clue to make a puzzle less hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Hint looks like part of the surface's clue-solving picture, but it is the verb meaning suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: To simplify is to make something less complicated, so easier to understand or do.

clue.text: President and film star entangled no more

indicators.note: entangled means twisted up together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A leader and an actress are no longer romantically involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the rumoured Kennedy and Marilyn affair, but the president is James Monroe.
explanation.definitionFit: James Monroe was the fifth US president and Marilyn Monroe a Hollywood star, so the surname fits both.

clue.text: Navy planes in dilapidated state

indicators.note: dilapidated means fallen into disrepair, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Naval aircraft in poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like part of 'dilapidated state', meaning condition; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennsylvania is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Common sense that's purposeless, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: something purposeless is of no use

explanation.surface: A cynic says practical wisdom is largely pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: NO USE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is an informal British word for practical intelligence or common sense.

clue.text: Part of speech some deliver brilliantly

indicators.note: some means a portion of the following words, so the answer is inside them

blocks.note: found across the end of deliver and the start of brilliantly

explanation.surface: A section of a speech that some people deliver superbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is one of the grammatical word classes known as parts of speech.

clue.text: Crow or rook evidently secured?

indicators.note: evidently signals that the clue shows the bird literally held inside the word for securing

blocks.note: to bag something is to secure it
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird in the crow family, perhaps caught and kept.
explanation.walkthrough: Crow and rook look like a pair of birds, but crow is the verb meaning boast. A bagged rook is R inside BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, the same as to brag.

clue.text: Reminder of holiday making one awfully envious, right?

indicators.note: awfully means in a terrible manner, so the letters are mangled

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone's holiday keepsake makes their friend jealous.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a memento kept to recall a place visited, typically on holiday.

clue.text: Raised fences every individual broke through

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the first word surrounds the next

blocks.note: to raise animals is to breed them
each means every individual one

explanation.surface: Livestock that were raised all broke out through the fences.
explanation.walkthrough: Fences looks like a noun in the farm picture; it is the verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To breach a wall or defence is to break through it.
